extracted.intended_audience: scientists, journal editors, and science-interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative points about who gets invited to peer review scientific papers, with emphasis on detecting and reducing gender and other demographic biases in reviewer suggestions and editorial practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should suggest gender-balanced reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists tend to suggest too few women as reviewers; male authors suggested female reviewers only 15 percent of the time while female authors suggested them 21 percent of the time, resulting in women making up only 20 percent of reviewers despite higher representation among members and first authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When suggesting reviewers, authors should aim for a gender mix that better reflects the pool of potential reviewers (e.g., membership or authorship proportions) rather than defaulting to predominantly male names. Be deliberate rather than relying on the first or easiest names that come to mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors should suggest and invite more women reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Male editors suggested women just 17 percent of the time and female editors 22 percent of the time, contributing to underrepresentation of women among reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should actively include women when composing reviewer invitation lists and monitor editor-suggested reviewer gender balance to avoid perpetuating gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase diversity in the editorial pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Push for more diversity in the journals' editorial pool — for gender, nationality and underrepresented minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widen the editor pool to include diverse backgrounds so the set of potential reviewer invitations and selections will be more diverse; improving editorial diversity is a systemic change that helps address reviewer-invitation bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and audit reviewer invitation demographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Merging datasets (authors, reviewers, editor- and author-named suggestions) enabled detection of gender bias in reviewer selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should collect and analyze data on reviewer invitations and completions by gender, age, and other demographics to detect disparities (e.g., percent female among suggested reviewers vs percent female in membership/authorship) and guide interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not let form design/timing create bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The time when authors are asked to suggest reviewers might play a role; the 'suggested reviewers' field is often last and filled when submitters are tired, which can magnify bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change submission form design and timing (e.g., move the reviewer-suggestion question earlier, provide prompts) to reduce hurried, heuristic choices that favor familiar (often male) names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide prompts/reminders to reduce biased heuristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Small things such as the order of fields and submitting when tired can cause biases because people rely on heuristics under time pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit prompts or reminders about diversity/opportunity gaps at the point of reviewer suggestion (e.g., 'Please consider suggesting qualified reviewers from underrepresented groups') to counteract default biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors should not over-rely on author-suggested reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may contact some recommended scientists and then reach out to a few more — over-reliance on author suggestions can perpetuate authors' biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should proactively seek additional reviewers beyond author suggestions, using objective searches and diversity-aware selection to ensure balanced invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize cumulative career impact of small biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Serving as a peer reviewer brings tangible benefits (learning, networking, CV credentials); small biases in reviewer invitations, if repeated, can have career-related effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reviewer-selection practices with awareness of cumulative opportunity disparities; prioritize equitable distribution of reviewing opportunities as part of career-development fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold authors and editors accountable through dialogue and awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting a dialog going for everyone to be aware of opportunity gaps and asking 'what can I do to make sure I'm not contributing to this' will be important to keep editors and authors aware and accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate conversations, trainings, and policies within journals and departments to raise awareness and create norms that discourage biased reviewer-selection behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid assuming age explains gender discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: The gender discrepancy in reviewer invitations persisted across age brackets, indicating it is not solely an age-related phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not justify underrepresentation of women reviewers by citing older cohorts; examine practices across all age groups and address systemic selection biases directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use research to test explanations for observed patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher acceptance rates for papers with female first authors prompted hypotheses (e.g., reverse discrimination) but required further investigation and skeptical interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When surprising patterns appear (such as differential acceptance rates), collect data and test hypotheses rather than assuming causation; use careful analysis to inform policy changes regarding reviewer selection or editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage local initiatives and training to sustain attention to bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting groups to discuss bias (as Lerback did) helps keep conversations going and maintain accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support grassroots and institutional efforts (reading groups, workshops, mentorship) that educate researchers about bias in reviewer selection and promote concrete practices to broaden reviewer pools.
